answer: The nurseryman raises seedlings bed by bed and writes the sowing date and the count in the bed book, so every plant is proved grown from seed. A pulse bed claimed as sown fails the book: the seedlings must have sprouted at the pigment of the bed, and a bed never sown shows bare soil. Faking a nursery season means hiring a nurseryman, buying seed and paying 7,900, while the mirror entry in the bed book is read at every planting, so seedlings whose bed was never sown are pulled up.
